logic.entry: At completed signal barj, upper=max(close[j-L:j]) and lower=min(close[j-10:j]), both exclude current signal bar. Compare Decimal close[j] with these strictly lagged levels. Track only successful entry fills at their next-day00:01UTC execution time; age is (current decision execution time minus that entry time)/86400000. Failed entries do not start the clock; failed exits preserve the existing clock. While flat, enter iff close[j]>upper; equality remains cash.
logic.exit: While long, exit first when filled-position age>=max_holding_days, otherwise when close[j]<min(previous exit_lookback_days closes excludingj). Lower-bound equality holds before timeout. No same-decision re-entry; terminal liquidation remains costed.
logic.sizing: Independent 2,000 USDT cash account; all original capital allocated to this asset; long-only, no leverage, no borrowing, no cross-asset transfer or add-on.
logic.timing: Close-based signal only from a closed UTC daily bar, next day 00:01 UTC one-minute open (60-second delay); no historical fill before OOS.

parameters.impact_model: 0.5 * sample_stdev(previous 20 complete UTC daily log returns) * sqrt(order quote budget / previous 20 complete daily quote-volume ADV)

sources.scope: Primary channel reference uses high/low extrema. Our generated close-only lagged channel is explicitly a different rule, not a literal replication or a profitability endorsement.
Time-based exit example tracks the executed entry timestamp. Our daily next-minute model retains a60second signal delay and does not use their same-close immediate order example.
Official filter definitions; historical filters remain unavailable.
